title: Ethiopian Dessert Platter
community: All of Ethiopia — the complete sweet experience
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Dessert Platter — the complete Ethiopian sweet experience. Honey Cookies (ETH191), Sesame Candy (ETH198), Coconut Balls (ETH203), Coffee Truffles (ETH202), Honey Banana (ETH196), Date Cake (ETH197), and the Ethiopian Fruit Platter (ETH200) on one celebration table.
longDesc: The Ethiopian Dessert Platter is the sweet conclusion to the great feast — assembling the finest Ethiopian sweets in one presentation that moves from ancient (sesame candy, honey cookies) to modern (coffee truffles) and from simple (coconut balls) to elaborate (date cake).
steps: Days before: make honey cookies, sesame candy, coconut balls, date cake — all keep well.
Day of: prepare fruit platter. Make honey bananas to order.
Assemble on a large board: sweets in centre, fruit at edges, warm bananas in a dish.
chefTips: The dry sweets (cookies, candy, coconut balls) can all be made well ahead.
Coffee truffles are the sophisticated centrepiece.
Honey bananas should be served warm — make last.
commonMistakes: Attempting the honey bananas ahead of time.
sustainabilityTips: The Ethiopian dessert platter uses Ethiopian honey, sesame, teff, and fruit — entirely locally sourced.
servedWith: At the conclusion of any Ethiopian celebration feast
healthBenefits: Ethiopian sweets use honey rather than refined sugar as the primary sweetener — providing antioxidants, antimicrobial compounds, and a lower glycaemic impact than pure sugar confections.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian Dessert Platter is the sweet proof that Ethiopian food culture extends to dessert with the same depth and variety as its main courses — ancient and modern, simple and complex, honey and chocolate, sesame and coffee. It is Ethiopia's sweet soul on one table.
